name: Lofexidine
summary: Lofexidine, sold under the brand name Lucemyra among others, is a medication historically used to treat high blood pressure; today, it is more commonly used to help with the physical symptoms of opioid withdrawal. It is taken by mouth. It is an α2A-adrenergic receptor agonist. It was approved for use by the Food and Drug Administration in the United States in 2018, considering it to be a first-in-class medication.

pharmacology.text: Lofexidine is an agonist at the alpha-2A, 2B, and 2C adrenergic receptor subtypes, with the highest activity at the α2A-adrengergic receptor. Ki represents the dissociation constant for lofexidine's binding to a specific subtype of α2 receptor. The smaller the Ki value, the stronger the drug binds to the receptor to exert its activity.
